transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I got scared. I’ve been having thoughts like it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes driving home from the clinic, I catch myself wondering what would happen if I just didn’t turn the wheel.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not waking up or wondering what would happen if you didn't turn the wheel while driving?
About a month, I think. Since things got really intense with taking in our relative… it’s been kind of up and down since then.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time since you started having these thoughts?

Yeah… most days, I think. It’s like everything just feels kind of drained out. Even when the house is busy, I’ll go hide in the laundry room and cry because I don’t want anyone to see how hopeless I feel.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before these feelings started?

Not really. I used to take pictures, check the bird feeders, fuss over what was coming up in the garden… and lately I just haven’t cared. I haven’t even picked up my camera. It’s… unsettling, because those things were kind of how I felt like myself.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

Not really. I mean… I haven’t touched my camera, and even the bird feeders or the garden don’t really do anything for me right now. Those used to be the things I looked forward to, so… it’s kind of scary.
Have you experienced any periods where your depressive symptoms were significantly worse than others over the past month?
Yeah… I think so. It’s been kind of up and down, but this whole crisis around taking in our relative has been going on about a month, and some stretches have definitely felt worse.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how quickly you move compared to before these feelings started?

Yeah… my energy’s been really low. At work, just walking from the treatment area over to the lab benches feels like I’m dragging myself through mud. And when I get home, I’m pretty much done… I can barely get dinner together or help with the evening care routine.
Have you experienced any periods over the past month where you felt completely unable to take care of yourself or your daily responsibilities?

Yeah… there have been times like that. I’m still showing up, mostly, but I’ve been making mistakes at the clinic, and I’ve been avoiding people because I’m worried I’ll either snap or just… fall apart.

At home, my husband’s had to take over a lot — the bills, meals, kind of watching me when my thoughts get dark. I don’t like saying that, but… yes.
Have you felt like you're moving slower than usual or like your thoughts are slower?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I feel slowed down, but I don’t know if I’m actually moving slower. My head feels kind of foggy sometimes, I guess.
Have you been feeling restless or having trouble sitting still lately?

Yeah… a little. There were several days where after work I just couldn’t really sit still. I’d pace around the house, measuring rooms, making lists, reorganizing cabinets… staying up doing that after everyone else had gone to bed.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past month?

I haven’t really weighed myself, so I don’t know exactly. My appetite’s been… uneven. Lately I mostly just pick at toast or have coffee, and then I’ll get to the end of a clinic shift and realize I barely ate.
Have you been feeling like you're fidgeting or having trouble staying still when you're sitting or lying down?

Yes… sort of. I’d sit down and then get right back up to do something. I took extra shifts, redid our whole household care schedule, called contractors… tried to coordinate everybody’s tasks like it was some big hospital project. No one really asked me to, I just couldn’t leave it alone.
Have you felt like your body has been moving more slowly than usual?
Not really… I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself moving slower. If anything, I’m just… not sitting still much.
Have you been feeling an internal restlessness or agitation that makes you want to move around?

Yeah… I think so. It’s less like pacing for no reason and more like I can’t just leave things alone. I picked up extra shifts, redid the whole home care schedule, started calling contractors… kind of tried to run everyone’s tasks like a big hospital project. It was probably too much.
Have you been feeling like you need to keep moving or doing something, even when there's no real reason to?

Yes. For a few days after work I just… couldn’t settle. I’d be walking around the house, measuring rooms, making lists, rearranging cabinets, even late after everyone else was asleep. It didn’t really need doing.
Have you felt like you've been moving your body more than usual, like you can't sit still, over the past month?

Yes… for several days, after work especially, I just couldn’t sit still. I kept walking around the house, measuring things, making lists, reorganizing cabinets… even after everyone else had gone to bed.
Have you had any days over the past month where you felt completely normal and didn't experience any of these depressive thoughts or feelings?

No… not really. Most days it feels like everything’s kind of drained of color. Even when the house is busy, I just feel… hopeless. I try not to let anyone see it, so sometimes I end up crying in the laundry room.
Have you had any periods over the past month where your depressive symptoms were so severe that you couldn't get out of bed or leave the house?

Not exactly stuck in bed for days, but… it’s been bad enough that I’m not functioning right. I’ve made mistakes at the clinic, and I’ve been avoiding friends because I’m scared I’ll snap or just fall apart. At home, my husband’s been handling the bills and meals… and keeping an eye on me when my thoughts get dark.
Have you been feeling like you're fidgeting or having trouble staying still when you're sitting or lying down over the past week?
Yeah… a bit. Mostly after work. I’d sit down and then just get back up again, pacing around the house, making lists or moving things in cabinets. It went on pretty late some nights.
Have you had any periods over the past month where you felt so low that you thought you might be better off dead?

Yes… I have. I don’t really like saying it, but that’s part of why I came in. I keep thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And… sometimes driving home from the clinic, I catch myself wondering what would happen if I didn’t turn the wheel.
